label: copy-phase input token i
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L) when the fed-back input token is i, i.e. the model just output an i and is now recalling the next original token. Recall is 100% on dev; never fires on i during the original phase or on the delimiter step, and never on any other input token. About 20% of copy-phase i inputs stay inactive, mostly early in short sequences (t < 6, small L). Magnitude increases with recall position (lowest when i is the first original token, recall_idx 1). The largest activations come at late recall positions, often in runs of repeated i (the next token to output is also i).

issues: The core label and predicate hold up. On test, (phase==2)&(in_tok==i) has recall 1.0, mass recall 1.0, precision 0.80 and F1 0.889. Misses on test are 0 steps. The profile shows zero activation in the original and delimiter phases and on every in_tok other than i. 'Never fires on i during the original phase' is confirmed: orig_idx 0..8 all have 0 actives.

The explanation's account of the false positives is wrong. It says the inactive copy-phase i inputs are 'mostly early steps in short sequences (t < 6, small L)'. On test, the predicate restricted to t<6 has only 3302 predicted steps at precision 0.098, which is about 2,980 false positives. Restricted to t>=6 it has 87729 predicted steps at precision 0.826, which is about 15,240 false positives. So roughly 84% of the 18,221 test false positives are at t>=6. Misses output shows many of them at steps 9-14 with L=5..9, e.g. 's r l i y f 0 <DEL> s r l *i*' at step 11 and 'w f k x p i c <DEL> ... *i*' at step 13.

The false positives follow a graded pattern by out_tok, the token being output at that step. Dev precision of the predicate within each out_tok ranges from 0.46-0.53 for q, z and e, through about 0.67-0.72 for c, k, t and w, up to 0.95-0.97 for r and i. This looks like a soft magnitude modulation near the activation threshold rather than a separate class. Excluding the low-precision out_toks does not improve test F1 (0.862).

recall_idx==1 (the first fed-back token) has lower precision (0.67, dev), which fits the claim that magnitude is lowest there. Top activations are at late recall positions (6-8), and most are followed by or part of i-runs, which fits 'largest activations at late recall positions, often within runs of repeated i'.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate. The predicate is equivalent to 'fed-back i in the copy phase' (in_first==0 gives the same scores).
